subject: BrightCart — sudden throughput collapse & error spike (KV cache contention)
thread_summary: Customer BrightCart reported a rapid P99 latency and 5xx spike across their production routes. Investigation identified KV cache head-of-line blocking and aggressive LRU churn caused by a small number of long-lived batch requests. Temporary mitigations (lane isolation, per-key rate limits) were proposed and approved; next steps include a config rollout, deeper offline profiling, and an exec update recommending a one-week credit and a technical checkpoint.

Subject: Re: Fwd: [CRITICAL] production p99 jump + 502s — need immediate help

Short triage notes (initial):
- We see a sudden increase in KV cache miss/reinsert churn on the BrightCart tenant's hot key partition.
- Correlates with a small set (~12) of requests holding large KV prefixes for extended durations (batch-style requests). Those requests are tying up the hot-lane allocator and blocking other ISR (interactive small requests) lanes — classic HOL blocking.
- Observed increased kernel context switches and GPU queue backpressure on nodes serving the tenant.

Immediate mitigations I can push within 10 min (low-risk):
1) Per-tenant lane isolation: move BrightCart's low-priority batch lanes to separate lane class (preserve interactive lanes for checkout/search).
2) Short-term per-key rate limit: drop/queue long prefix requests above threshold (config-only).
3) Temporarily increase KV eviction aggressiveness for the tenant's hotset (reduces churn impact).

I'll prepare a config patch (kv-policy-diff.patch) for a rolling config rollout. We should hold off on restarts.

I'll attach basic traces and a short ops-runbook-link.txt to the thread once ready.

-Jasmine
SRE On-call, Runtime

Subject: Re: Fwd: [CRITICAL] production p99 jump + 502s — need immediate help

Summary of deeper analysis (10:50-09:10 run):
- Root cause (probable): Interaction between long-lived batch requests that pin wide prefixes and our LRU eviction combined with lane allocator exhaustion. The pinned prefixes cause frequent reinserts for hot keys and evict recently used small requests — leads to HOL blocking on hot-lane dispatcher.
- Why this surfaced now: BrightCart introduced a scheduled inventory-sync job earlier today that issues large multi-prefix batch lookups (not previously exercised at that scale).
- Quick mitigations accepted: Jasmine's three-step plan. I recommend we also add an immediate per-lane concurrency cap and reduce max-batch-size for the batch lane to lower lock contention.

Impact plan:
- T+10m: apply per-tenant lane isolation + per-key rate limit (config-only) — expected P99 improvement within 5-15m.
- T+30m: reduce batch-lane max size + apply concurrency cap.
- T+2h: offline profiling sweep + plan permanent policy changes (prefix isolation, tenant hotset reservations).

I'll run the rollout and watch the telemetry. If P99 isn't improved within 20m, we escalate to an exec briefing.

— Marissa Cole
Engineering Manager, Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai

Cc: ops@brightcart.com, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 27 Mar 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Executive note: BrightCart incident — immediate actions & recommendation

Team / Helen — quick exec-level note for records and approvals:

What happened (TL;DR): BrightCart hit a P99 latency and 5xx spike due to head-of-line blocking driven by a new large-scale inventory-sync job. The job pins wide prefixes in the KV cache while our lane allocator and LRU interact poorly, causing eviction churn and blocking short interactive requests.

Actions taken (completed / in-progress):
- T+10m: Rolled per-tenant lane isolation + per-key soft rate limits (config-only, rolling).
- T+20m: Reduced batch-lane max-batch-size and applied a per-lane concurrency cap.
- Telemetry: P99 improved from >1.6s to ~320ms within 12 minutes of the first change; error-rate dropped from 3.8% to 0.4%.

Proposed follow-ups (needs approval):
1) Overnight config persist and a full policy rollout to ensure batch lanes remain constrained for BrightCart's tenant (non-disruptive).
2) One-week customer goodwill credit (we recommend 10% of March invoice) — ops request + CS approval needed.
3) Engineering follow-up: schedule a workload isolation effort (prefix reservations, hotset capacity) and include BrightCart for a joint architecture review. Estimated 2 sprints.

I recommend we approve (1) and (2) now to close the loop with BrightCart and (3) as a commit in next sprint planning.

Ben — can you propose short customer messaging and confirm any commercial implications? Marissa/Jasmine — confirm the config diff so I can get legal/finance a one-pager if we agree on a credit.

— Dylan
Sr. Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
